moves.semantic-status-color: --signal-live #34e0a1, --signal-warn #ffcf5c, --signal-crit #ff4d6d encode live/warning/critical states; .presence beacon-pulse uses live signal color for presence
moves.expressive-accent: --accent #ff4d1f and --accent-hot #ff7a3d saturated orange; elev-dramatic shadow bleeds accent: 0 24px 64px -16px rgba(255,77,31,0.2); comment 'expressive type on a dark ground'
moves.restrained-neutral-chrome: deep neutral ground/surface ramp (--ground #080b12 through --surface-2 #1b2233, --edge #232c40) and text ramp text-hi/mid/dim ground the chrome; focal object uses NEUTRAL ink shadow with 'hue lives on marking'

catalog.label: tabular-mono-numerals
catalog.what: Numbers line up in fixed-width columns so live readings stay steady and don't jitter as values change.
catalog.evidence: BeaconMono labels use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for aligned numeric data

catalog.label: lit-focal-object-color-separation
catalog.what: The main object stays a neutral dark tone, so color is saved only for signals and markers.
catalog.evidence: material comment 'the lit focal object' with top-lit gradient (#1b2233→#0d1119), bevel highlights and neutral dramatic float shadow — deliberately keeps the focal object neutral so hue is reserved for signal/entity marking

catalog.label: ambient-radar-loop
catalog.what: A radar-like beam sweeps continuously around the display in a slow, endless rotation.
catalog.evidence: @keyframes beacon-sweep { from rotate(0deg) to rotate(360deg) } applied to the .sweep conic-gradient field as a perpetual anchor animation

catalog.label: perpetual-marquee
catalog.what: A ticker strip drifts sideways nonstop, always moving regardless of whether anything has actually changed.
catalog.evidence: @keyframes signal-drift translateX(0) to translateX(-50%) on the .ticker — a continuously drifting base ticker with no state change

catalog.label: confidence-meter
catalog.evidence: No `.conf` bar or any proportional fill for confidence exists in the product; the confidence row renders only a value cell.
catalog.instead: a plain text data-row that lists confidence alongside origin/vector/eta

catalog.label: icon-glyphs
catalog.evidence: The product uses no glyph affordances (no ×, no › chevron) anywhere — close is a worded button and rows carry no chevron marker.
catalog.instead: a text label ("CLOSE") standing in for the dismiss glyph

catalog.label: status-badge
catalog.evidence: No `.badge` class, chip, or bordered status pill appears anywhere in the product — searched CSS, inline style; status surfaces only as raw text.
catalog.instead: inline colored status text next to the signal id, reinforced by the hue of the presence dot

catalog.label: sync-bar
catalog.evidence: No `.syncbar` or any width-driven fill meter for sync exists in the product; sync appears only as a number in the drifting ticker string.
catalog.instead: inline percentage text in the ticker

catalog.label: timed-arm-commit
catalog.what: A single click arms, then self-advances through stages before opening, instead of toggling instantly.
catalog.evidence: activate() pushes a sequence of timers: setPhase('committed') at ARM, then setOpen(true)/setPhase('idle') at ARM+BEAT — a single click drives a self-progressing phase machine ('idle'→'committed'→open) rather than an instant toggle, with onClick={open ? dismiss : activate} switching behavior once armed.

catalog.label: pointer-scrub-track
catalog.what: Dragging along a track continuously sets a value as you move, scrubbing smoothly with your finger or cursor.
catalog.evidence: onPointerDown captures the pointer (setPointerCapture) and sets held; onPointerMove={(e)=>held && scrubTo(e.clientX)} maps continuous pointer X position along a track ref to scrubT; onPointerUp releases — dragging along an axis continuously sets a scalar value.

catalog.label: top-lit-directional-bevel
catalog.what: Surfaces look lit from above, with a bright top edge and a cool shadow below.
catalog.evidence: Explicit comment '/* lighting: lit from the top, falling into cool shadow */' with box-shadow combining 'inset 0 2px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.10) /* bevel: top edge catches light */' and 'inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.55)' — a directional two-edge inset bevel simulating a consistent overhead light source, distinct from a plain recessed inset.

_checklist: COMPOSITION — organize around a central-canvas spine.  WHY: When the work is to grasp many live signals at once, a single immersive field keeps everything in view while details surface in context rather than replacing the whole.

TYPOGRAPHY — carry the moves ['custom-display-face', 'distinct-body-face', 'expressive-weight', 'extreme-scale-contrast', 'treated-microtype', 'type-as-graphic'] · DEPLOYMENT: reserve ['custom-display-face', 'expressive-weight', 'extreme-scale-contrast', 'treated-microtype', 'type-as-graphic'] for the focal moments — the source deploys sparingly ('custom-display-face' in ~20% of source files, 'expressive-weight' in ~20% of source files, 'extreme-scale-contrast' in ~20% of source files, 'treated-microtype' in ~20% of source files, 'type-as-graphic' in ~20% of source files); a reserved move applied everywhere stops reading as identity.  WHY: When readings must be grasped at a glance, type that dramatizes scale and voice lets the vital numbers register instantly while labels recede into quiet support.

COLOR — carry the moves ['entity-driven-color', 'expressive-accent', 'semantic-status-color'] · APPLICATION: keep ['semantic'] color to marking (data/text/interactive), never flood it onto surfaces · ground is DARK (tonality 0.08) — match that polarity.  WHY: When color is derived from what's being observed and encodes meaning, the person reads state at a glance instead of decoding a legend.

DENSITY — carry the moves ['floating-overlays', 'full-bleed-canvas', 'generous-hero-space'].  WHY: when the view fills the whole surface and content breathes, the operator reads the full field of signals at a glance without a frame competing for attention.

_guide.deployment_frequency: An identity move has a HOME. Carrying a move does NOT mean maximizing it: the source deploys its strongest moves — textures, glows, loops, display type — at a specific frequency (the checklist's DEPLOYMENT notes give the observed rate), and that restraint is itself part of the identity. Applying a reserved move to every element destroys the figure/ground contrast that makes it read as identity; the build goes noisy and one-dimensional, and the gate flags clear over-application. Match the deployment pattern, not just the move.
_guide.omission_is_identity: What the product LEAVES OUT is as binding as what it adds. Agents reach for their defaults — shadows, icons, toasts, spinners, confirm dialogs, hover lifts — and each one quietly erodes an identity built on refusing it. Every SUBTRACTION on the checklist is a requirement, not a gap to fill; if a need seems to demand the omitted thing, use the product's substitute instead.
_guide.build_to_the_why: The checklist's WHY clauses are the product's dispositions — its soul. Build to those principles, not just to pass the checks. A check is a floor, not the finish: passing conformance means you didn't violate the grammar, NOT that it feels like one designer's hand.
build_order: 1. SKELETON — stand up the composition spine and the focal object first (structure before style). A great skin on no spine reads as generic.
2. MATERIAL — give the focal object its layered material (the SURFACE moves).
3. BEHAVIOR — bind the interaction grammar (gesture → response) on the component roles.
4. STYLE — carry each facet's moves at the stated MAGNITUDE (as loud as the source, not a tasteful echo).
5. POLISH — the craft below. This is where a passing build becomes a good one.

you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.note: Static analysis reads declared DOM/CSS, not the rendered/animated result. These are real identity but UNVERIFIABLE — a green report does NOT cover them, so they are yours to get right by hand.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.motion_smoothness: Real easing and staged timing — no linear tweens, no jank. Animate transform/opacity, not layout. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.color_harmony: The palette must read as ONE system — even lightness/chroma steps, restrained hue families. Passing the color moves ≠ a harmonious palette.
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.type_layout: Clean arrangement — aligned to a grid, consistent vertical rhythm, a hierarchy that reads. (Rich size vocabularies are fine; sloppy ARRANGEMENT is not.)
you_own_these_the_gate_cannot_check.material_feel: Glossy vs flat, focal richness — the rendered richness the layer/alpha counts can't distinguish. Make the focal object look genuinely lit.

_guide.reading_the_gate: The gate is DETERMINISTIC except color, which is semantic (marking-vs-decoration is a judgment about meaning). Consequences: (a) a FAIL that stays IDENTICAL on UNCHANGED code is REAL — fix the build, do not re-run hoping it clears, and do not contort code to game a signature. (b) The color check can shift between edits because it re-reads meaning; trust a stable verdict on unchanged code. (c) 'accent decorates instead of marks' is about MEANING: a colored glow on a data entity MARKS (good); a decorative gradient DECORATES (flagged).
